title: introduce-idempotency-lease-and-retry-advice-header-for-streamed-tools
author: Aditi Rao
release_notes: Adds idempotency lease header and X-Redwood-Retry-Advice for streamed tool calls; introduces a compact 429/503 error envelope for stream frames and documents migration guidance for OpenAI-compat consumers.
description: Motivation: streaming tool invocations (function calls / tool calls) have shown intermittent duplicate execution under retry scenarios where clients reconnected or replayed frames without clear guidance from the server. Current retry semantics rely on ad-hoc idempotency headers and ambiguous 429/Retry-After interactions, which complicates client implementations (especially OpenAI-compatible shims). This PR introduces a coordinated server-side lease for in-flight tool executions plus a machine-readable retry advice header to make client retry logic explicit and robust. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a short-lived idempotency lease header X-Redwood-Idempotency-Lease (opaque token) returned on successful tool invocation acceptance. The lease encodes a server-side lease duration and execution id metadata so subsequent reconnects/replays can be correlated and deduplicated. 2) Add X-Redwood-Retry-Advice header for requests that are throttled or failed due to transient capacity (429/503). The header contains a comma-separated advisory payload: "window_ms=xxx,backoff_hint_ms=yyy,scope=soft|hard". It is not a strict instruction but a machine-consumable hint clients can use to schedule reconnection/backoff and choose whether to re-send payloads or rely on the idempotency lease. 3) Introduce a compact, stable error envelope for streamed frames (content-type application/vnd.redwood.error+json) that standardizes error codes (rate_limit, transient_capacity, invalid_input, auth) and includes fields: code, message, retry_advice (mirrors header), and lease_token (if available). This reduces ambiguity when streaming where HTTP-level headers are insufficient once the connection is established. 4) Server-side handling: when a tool call is accepted we issue a lease token and persist a small execution record keyed by execution id for the lease window (default 30s). Retries/reconnects presenting the same lease token will be acknowledged as duplicate and emit a replay-ack frame instead of re-executing. 5) OpenAI-compat adapter: map legacy OpenAI idempotency_key semantics to the new lease when possible; when an incoming request contains OpenAI-style Idempotency-Key we translate to a lease and emit X-Redwood-Idempotency-Lease for downstream OpenAI-compat clients to consume. 6) Backwards compatibility: clients that do not understand the new headers continue to work — the server will still return existing 429/Retry-After responses. Migration guidance included below. Commits (high level): [commit 1] runtime: add lease store and expiration policy for streamed tool executions [commit 2] runtime: emit X-Redwood-Idempotency-Lease on accepted tool frames [commit 3] api: implement X-Redwood-Retry-Advice header and header formatter [commit 4] streaming-protocol: define application/vnd.redwood.error+json envelope and wire to frames [commit 5] openai-compat: translate Idempotency-Key into lease token and surface header [commit 6] tests: unit + integration test for lease replay handling + CI harness update [commit 7] docs: migration guide and console FAQ update Changed files (high level): - core/runtime/lease_store.go: new in-memory/redis-backed lease store with TTL and instrumentation - core/runtime/handler_stream_tool.go: logic for issuing lease tokens, detecting replays, returning replay-ack frames - pkg/http/headers.go: helpers for header serialization/parsing - api/compat/openai/adapter.go: translation layer for Idempotency-Key -> lease token - streaming/protocol/errors.go: new error envelope definition and serializers - docs/migrations/idempotency-lease.md: migration guide and examples - tests/integration/stream-leases.test: new integration test scenarios Testing and verification: unit tests cover lease lifecycle, duplicate-detection semantics, and header formatting. Integration tests simulate network reconnects, partial frame delivery, and client replay to ensure no double execution within lease window; CI run included e2e against openai-compat shim. Performance: minimal overhead for accepted calls — lease creation is an O(1) insert with TTL. Benchmarks show ~1.2% p99 latency increase for single-call acceptance at 1k/s, but avoids larger latency and cost from duplicate executions under noisy networks. Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag lease.enabled (false by default). We will enable rollout in Canary first (internal pods) for 48h, escalate to progressive rollout with monitoring for duplicate-execution metric and overall tail-latency. Migration notes for clients: - Optional: prefer X-Redwood-Idempotency-Lease (if present) when deciding to replay frames or re-send tool payloads. - Use X-Redwood-Retry-Advice to tune retry timers; if scope=hard, defer resubmit until after window_ms. - OpenAI-compat clients: client libraries that accept Idempotency-Key will be able to read back X-Redwood-Idempotency-Lease for deterministic handling. Review conversation (summary): Reviewer Evan Liu: "Nice narrow scope. Two concerns: (1) lease token size and perf — can we make it compact and base64? (2) race where lease expired between client reconnect and server handling — what's the expected error?" Author (Aditi): "Lease is opaque base64 of 20 bytes (nonce + short encoding). On expiry we return error envelope with code transient_capacity and retry_advice advising a new backoff window. Added tests for expiry races." Reviewer Priya Kapoor: "Header grammar looks good; please add JSON schema examples in docs and include client pseudo-code." Author: "Added examples and pseudo-code in docs/migrations/idempotency-lease.md." Reviewer Samir Desai: "OpenAI compat path — are we leaking Idempotency-Key values in logs?" Author: "No, adapter redacts original keys before logging and only logs hashed IDs; updated audit logs to avoid materializing raw keys." Approvals: Evan Liu approved, Priya Kapoor approved, Samir requested small follow-up that was shipped. CI: initial flaky test in integration (timeout) was increased and rerun; final CI green. Merge: squash-merged to main on 2026-02-17 with release note entry and migration doc published. Operational runbooks: added short runbook for investigating duplicate-execution spikes and how to toggle lease.enabled and tune lease_window_ms. Known limitations: - Lease window is intentionally short (default 30s); long-running tools may need additional coordination (follow-up ticket ENG-1522). - Not suitable as sole dedupe mechanism for requests that must survive long offline periods. Follow-ups: ENG-1522 (extend lease semantics for long-running tools), ENG-1530 (client library helpers for Node/Python to parse retry advice header).
